explanation: Scan characters once, extending a token through letters and valid internal punctuation. Normalize each completed token to lowercase and increment its dictionary entry.
correctness: Each maximal sequence satisfying the disclosed token grammar is emitted once. Lowercasing maps permitted case variants to the same dictionary key, and one increment per token gives its occurrence count.
walkthrough: For "Owls fly; OWLS don't crawl. Fly-by owls!", punctuation ends tokens but internal apostrophes and letter-surrounded hyphens remain. Lowercasing combines Owls, OWLS and owls into count 3. The other keys are fly, don't, crawl and fly-by, each counted once under the disclosed bank policy.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n text characters.
spaceComplexity: O(n) result storage; one growing dictionary plus the current token.
